clue.text: Recurrent saying in busy pubs?

indicators.note: in places the turned saying inside the mixed-up letters
busy suggests bustle and jumbling, so the letters of pubs are mixed up
recurrent read as running back on itself, so the saying is written backwards

parts.note: a motto is a short saying

explanation.surface: A toast heard over and over again in crowded bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurrent' reads backwards the word for the saying, and 'busy' scrambles PUBS around it. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the toast itself, so it is an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: This drinking toast, urging everyone to drain their glasses, is repeated endlessly in a lively bar.

clue.text: First to burst flaccid balloon

indicators.note: first to picks just the opening letter of the word burst

parts.note: flaccid means limp, floppy

explanation.surface: A balloon that pops first ends up limp and deflated.
explanation.definitionFit: A blimp is a non-rigid airship, an elongated balloon.

clue.text: Present for discussion on second key food additive

parts.note: to table a motion is to put it forward for discussion
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A motion about a key ingredient is put up for debate at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Common salt is sprinkled into or onto food as a seasoning, an additive.

clue.text: Gracious Evita reportedly turned up to embrace workers

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
to embrace says the words hold the answer's letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Eva Perón is said to have appeared graciously to hug labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'embrace workers' as the definition, but 'to embrace' is the hidden-word signal and only 'workers' defines. In a down clue 'turned up' reads the run SEVITAREPO from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatives are factory hands or agents, people who work.

clue.text: Collage of Matisse showing least variation

indicators.note: a collage is a cut-up and reassembled picture, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Matisse cut-out that is the most uniform of his works.
explanation.walkthrough: Matisse made famous paper cut-out collages late in life, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Samiest is the superlative of samey, most monotonous and unvaried.

clue.text: A supporter of mine

parts.note: reads like a fan backing me, but means a timber prop holding up a coal mine's roof

explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a beam that supports the roof in a mine shaft or tunnel.

clue.text: Oddly shunned, said piteous goodbye

indicators.note: shunning the odd letters leaves only the even-placed ones of said piteous

explanation.surface: Someone avoided, strangely, gave a pathetic farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, used in English to mean farewell.

clue.text: Pain of brill swallowing tip of hook

indicators.note: swallowing means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: brill is slang for brilliant, as is ace

indicators.note: tip of picks the first letter of hook

explanation.surface: A fish, the brill, suffers after gulping down an angler's hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like the flatfish but is slang for 'brilliant'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull, lasting pain.

clue.text: Sluggish ferrets regularly found beneath home

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters from ferrets sit below the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of ferrets

explanation.surface: Lazy pet ferrets are discovered lying under the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means inactive, slow to move.

clue.text: Draw peacekeepers' fire with high explosive

parts.note: the UN supplies peacekeepers; the possessive gives UN's
fire means heat, as in the heat of the fire

explanation.surface: Peacekeepers come under fire from explosives and draw their own weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins HE on the end; it is part of that leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a sword is to pull it from its scabbard.

clue.text: Suffuse disrobed limbs with beginnings of unalloyed eroticism

indicators.note: disrobed strips the outer letters off limbs, leaving the middle
beginnings of takes the first letter of each of unalloyed and eroticism

explanation.surface: Naked limbs filled with pure eroticism: a racy line.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to saturate or permeate, so the two verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Consummate marriage? Not so!

parts.note: a match is a marriage
less read as the suffix meaning without, denying what came before

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to consummate a marriage and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consummate' looks like a verb about marriage but is the adjective meaning supreme.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means perfect, unrivalled, without equal.

clue.text: Accommodation and clothing denied to French revolutionary over time

indicators.note: over means the shortened name covers the word for time on both sides
denied to means the clothing is taken away from the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Robespierre was a leader of the French Revolution's Terror
robes are clothing
a date is a point in time

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary is refused lodging and clothes for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French revolutionary' wants to be a separate figure, but the clothing (robes) is stripped from Robespierre's own name, and 'over' wraps what is left, PIERRE, round the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-a-terre is a small second home kept for occasional stays.

clue.text: Filthy place ultimately became eyesore

parts.note: a sty, the pigs' pen, is a byword for squalor

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of became

explanation.surface: A grubby spot ended up an eyesore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' reads as an ugly sight but is literally a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on an eyelid, literally a sore eye.

clue.text: Maiden, with tact, ordered entree

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman, tactfully, has chosen the main course from the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entree' and 'ordered' suggest a restaurant, but entree here means right of entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is the right to enter, which is permission to come in.

clue.text: Conveyance of gas round back of Number 10

indicators.note: round means the chat word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to gas is to chatter, to chat

indicators.note: back of takes the last letter of Number

parts.note: 10 looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Gas is piped round the back of Number 10 Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 10 Downing Street is the UK prime minister's home.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn vehicle, a means of transport.

clue.text: Alliance of nearly everybody in Congress

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word inside the other

parts.note: congress can mean sexual intercourse, coition

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: everybody means all

explanation.surface: A coalition backed by nearly every member of the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' is not the legislature but sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is a union of parties working together, a pact.

clue.text: Spooner's fake history published on the internet

indicators.note: Spooner's says to swap the opening sounds, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: cod means sham or mock, as in cod history
the past is history

explanation.surface: A bogus history is put online.
explanation.definitionFit: To podcast is to issue an audio show online as a download; here it is the past participle.

clue.text: Turn red, sat awkwardly on top with a leg on each side

definitions.text: with a leg on each side

indicators.note: in a down clue the jumbled letters sit above the other piece
awkwardly means these letters are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: to raddle is to colour with red ochre

explanation.surface: Someone blushes, sitting clumsily astride something.
explanation.walkthrough: Raddle is red ochre, rubbed on rams so they mark the ewes they mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Astraddle means straddling, sitting with legs either side.

clue.text: Port went off, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: RP is Received Pronunciation, the standard British accent

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters of went are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fortified wine went bad, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine, which 'went off' supports; it is the Belgian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's largest seaports.

clue.text: Criminal cartel headed by leader of pheasant pluckers

indicators.note: in a down clue the leader's letter is at the head of the rest
leader of takes the first letter of pheasant
criminal suggests bent, so the letters of cartel are twisted

explanation.surface: A crime gang run by the boss of the game-bird pluckers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluckers' reads as people who pluck birds, but means what plucks guitar strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plectra, plural of plectrum, are picks for strumming strings.

clue.text: Quietly handle extremely rare love potion

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a hilt is the handle of a sword

indicators.note: extremely takes the two end letters of rare

explanation.surface: Someone is told to handle a very rare aphrodisiac quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a magic drink meant to make someone fall in love.

clue.text: Surreptitiously photograph your American manuscript

parts.note: to pap is to snap like paparazzi
yr is the short written form of your

explanation.surface: Covertly snap a page of your American's handwritten text.
explanation.definitionFit: A papyrus is an ancient document written on reed paper.

clue.text: Left-wingers in Italian towns campaigned hard and long

indicators.note: the left wings of the words are their first letters, read across

explanation.surface: Communists in Italian towns ran a hard and lengthy campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-wingers' looks political, but the left edges of the next four words give the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to yearn for it.

clue.text: Memory of country singer on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio signals that the name is heard rather than read

parts.note: Johnny Cash was a country music star

explanation.surface: Memories of a country star played on air.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a cache is a fast memory store.

clue.text: Are responsible for Her Majesty meeting Blue Peter dog in private

indicators.note: in places the queen and dog inside the soldier

parts.note: Pte is the army abbreviation for private
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
Petra was the dog on the BBC children's show Blue Peter

explanation.surface: The Queen meets a TV dog privately, and someone is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Peter is a long-running BBC children's TV show, whose first dog was Petra. 'meeting' just joins ER and PETRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate is to commit a deed; plural verb matching plural subject.

clue.text: Each is ruefully discontented after night before

indicators.note: after puts the letters from ruefully behind the evening word

parts.note: an eve is the evening before an event

indicators.note: discontented empties ruefully of its contents, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: Everyone is regretful and fed up after a big night.
explanation.definitionFit: Every and each both pick out all members of a group one by one.

clue.text: Old boyfriend said to be member of orchestra

indicators.note: said means the pieces are spoken and heard

parts.note: O stands for old and a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: A former lover is rumoured to play in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument found in orchestras.

clue.text: Where Communists alone are elected to run neonatal facility

parts.note: in Cuba only the Communist Party may stand
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A place where only Communists win elections runs a baby unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Premature babies are kept in a heated box, a hospital unit for newborns.

clue.text: Drug finally injected into bare elbow

indicators.note: injected into puts one letter inside the other word

parts.note: bare means naked, nude

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Drug

explanation.surface: A drug is injected into a bare arm at the elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elbow' looks like a noun but is the verb to poke.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge is to prod someone with your elbow.

clue.text: Decent sandwiches start to entice relative

indicators.note: sandwiches means one word encloses the letter

parts.note: decent means nice, pleasant

indicators.note: start to takes the first letter of entice

explanation.surface: Pleasant sandwiches are a lure for a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Depend on Jane name-dropping without ostentation

indicators.note: name-dropping means N, short for name, is removed

parts.note: Jane Austen, the English novelist
depend on means rely

explanation.surface: Relying on a novelist while dropping names, with no showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Austerely means plainly, severely, without frills.
